name: Today's Report
headline: Rates are holding at 7.07% for now, but the 10-Year just closed at 4.95%, its highest since at least January 2024, and the Fed meets Wednesday with a hike priced in.
teaser: Mortgage News Daily still has the 30-year at 7.07% and the 15-year at 6.62%, Thursday's readings and the highest in at least a year. Friday's numbers post around 1 PM PT, and the setup is not friendly: the 10-Year jumped 0.12 on Thursday to 4.95%, and mortgage rates follow the 10-Year.

sections.label: Real estate
sections.html:
Mortgage News Daily still has the 30-year at 7.07% and the 15-year at 6.62%, Thursday's readings and the highest in at least a year. Friday's numbers post around 1 PM PT, and the setup is not friendly: the 10-Year jumped 0.12 on Thursday to 4.95%, and mortgage rates follow the 10-Year.

The reason sits in the Economy section. Wholesale prices ran hot, and traders now put 85.6% odds on a quarter-point Fed hike next Wednesday, per CME FedWatch. The Fed does not set mortgage rates, but it keeps the pressure on the bond yields that do.

  • The local math: at Fremont's median list price of $1,249,000, a 20% down loan is $999,200, which is jumbo. At MND's jumbo 30-year of 7.20%, principal and interest run about $6,782 a month.
  • Every eighth of a point on that loan is about $85 a month, which is why rate lock timing matters more than usual next week.

Alameda County (Fremont Focus)

  • Board wide: 2,760 listings across our 15 city table, counting active and in contract together, with 187 coming soon and 255 brand new.
  • Five city ledger: 720 live listings across Fremont, Hayward, Milpitas, Newark and Union City. 631 are already on the market and 89 are coming soon.
  • Fremont: 272 live, 206 active, 37 coming soon, 29 brand new. The median on market list price is $1,249,000 at $825 a square foot, and the typical active listing has been out 25 days.
  • The rest of the ledger: Hayward 183, Milpitas 123, Newark 88, Union City 54.
  • Across all five cities the median is $1,098,888 at $698 a square foot. 278 homes are priced under a million, and 156 have been sitting 60 days or longer.

What this means for you: supply jumped by 24 in a day, to 720 live listings from 696, with 115 arriving in the past week, so buyers have more to choose from. The pressure is on the payment, not the selection. Buyers in contract should talk to their lender about locking before Wednesday's Fed decision. For sellers, 156 homes past the 60 day mark says price for a 7% market.

sections.label: Economy
sections.html:
Wholesale prices are the story. The Producer Price Index rose 0.4% in August and 5.4% over the past year. Energy drove the month: final demand energy rose 4.2%, diesel jumped 24.1%, and BLS says energy accounted for over three fourths of the rise in goods prices.

Today's chart is the second one making the rounds, and its numbers are right. The headline, energy did the heavy lifting, is true of August. It is less true of the year: take out food, energy and trade and producer prices are still up 4.7%, and services are up 4.5%, both more than twice the Fed's 2% goal. Our version adds services and the month's detail so both halves show. The Fed's goal is for consumer prices, so read it as a yardstick.

That is why markets moved toward a hike, not a cut. The Fed meets next Wednesday, and CME FedWatch puts the odds of a quarter-point increase at 85.6%, up from 48.4% on August 11. The 10-Year jumped to 4.95%, its highest close since at least January 2024.

Oil kept climbing. Brent settled at $107.63 on Thursday, up 6.3% and its highest settlement since May 19, as Iran said it was ready for a wider conflict after the U.S. destroyed five of its tankers. It eased to about $104.74 Friday morning. Metals went the other way: at Thursday's 1:00 PM PT print gold fell 2.0% to $4,358.50 and silver 5.6% to $64.09, and both were bouncing Friday morning.

A note on the newsletter's numbers: its stock, rate and PPI figures check out, including diesel's 24% jump. It had the 10-Year at 4.96% against Treasury's 4.95%, gold down 2.29% where the same time prints show 1.99%, and Brent at $108.63, up 7.28%, against the $107.63 settlement, up 6.34%. Silver was omitted again.

images.alt: Bar chart of producer price changes over the 12 months through August 2026: energy 24.4%, all final demand 5.4%, core excluding food, energy and trade 4.7%, services 4.5%, against the Fed's 2% goal for consumer prices.
images.caption: Energy led August, rising 4.2% in the month with diesel up 24.1%. Over the year, producer prices excluding food, energy and trade are still up 4.7%, more than twice the Fed's 2% goal.
images.source: Source: U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics, Producer Price Index for August 2026, released September 10, 2026. 12 month changes are unadjusted.

sections.label: Stocks
sections.html:
Twenty-five years ago today, nearly 3,000 people lost their lives in the September 11 attacks. We remember them, their families, and the first responders.

Thursday made it four losing sessions in a row, each index down about six tenths of a percent. Friday opened with a bounce, all three up about 1% by mid morning.

Taiwan Semiconductor had the record of the day. TSMC's August revenue came in at NT$514.8 billion, up 53.3% from a year ago and 10.1% above July, its fourth straight monthly gain and its first month above NT$500 billion. That is about US$16.1 billion at August's average exchange rate of 32.0 Taiwan dollars per dollar; the newsletter's $16.4 billion assumes a stronger Taiwan dollar. AI chip demand is the whole story.

Today's chart is the one making the rounds, and its numbers check out to the cent: TSM closed Thursday at $428.03, up 40.9% from its December 31 close of $303.89. Our version adds the two things the original leaves out: the baseline that 41% is measured from, and the fact that the stock is still 10.4% below its June 30 high of $477.57. The shares were up about 1.6% Friday morning.

images.alt: Line chart of Taiwan Semiconductor (TSM) daily closing prices from December 31, 2025 to September 10, 2026, rising from $303.89 to $428.03, up 40.9%, with a June 30 high of $477.57 and a March 30 low of $316.50.
images.caption: TSM closed Thursday at $428.03, up 40.9% on the year and still 10.4% below its June 30 high. August revenue was a record NT$514.8 billion, up 53.3%.
images.source: Source: TSM daily closing prices via Yahoo Finance; TSMC monthly revenue report, August 2026.

sections.label: Crypto
sections.html:
Live quotes pulled at 9:00 AM PT with 24 hour changes. All three are higher with Friday's bounce, and Ether leads, up almost 5%.

Nasdaq is buying into crypto plumbing. Its venture arm is putting $100 million into Payward, the parent of the Kraken exchange, at a $21 billion valuation, to distribute tokenized versions of Nasdaq-listed stocks with a launch planned for 2027. Tokens are blockchain versions of shares that can trade around the clock.

Washington gets its turn Tuesday. The Senate holds a procedural vote on the Clarity Act, the bill that would decide which regulator oversees which coins and exchanges, and it needs 60 votes to move forward, which means it needs some Democrats.
